Color

contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

Navigation drawers provide access to destinations and app functionality, such as switching accounts. They can either be permanently on-screen or opened and closed by a navigation menu icon. One navigation destination is always active.

Navigation drawers are recommended for:

  • Apps with 5 or more top-level destinations
  • Apps with 2 or more levels of navigation hierarchy
  • Quick navigation between unrelated destinations
  • Replacing the navigation rail or navigation bar on large screens

contentChunks.footer: Use a navigation drawer for 5 or more primary destinations, or more than 1 level of navigation hierarchy
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer with multiple destinations in a mail app.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Avoid using a navigation drawer with other primary navigation components, such as a navigation bar.

Instead, choose a single navigation component based on product requirements and breakpoints:

  • Navigation bars for compact breakpoints

  • Navigation rails for medium and expanded breakpoints 

  • Standard navigation drawers for expanded, large and extra-large breakpoints

contentChunks.footer: Avoid using two navigation components on the same screen
contentChunks.altText: Standard navigation drawer and navigation bar used together.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
There are two variants of navigation drawers:

  1. Standard navigation drawer

  2. Modal navigation drawer

contentChunks.footer: Standard navigation drawer
contentChunks.altText: Standard navigation drawer with destinations in mail app.

contentChunks.footer: Modal navigation drawer
contentChunks.altText: Modal navigation drawer with destinations and scrim.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Standard navigation drawer

Standard navigation drawers provide access to drawer destinations and app content for layouts in expanded, large, and extra-large breakpoints. 

Standard drawers can be permanently visible (best for frequently switching destinations) or opened and closed by tapping a menu icon (best for focusing more on screen content).

In medium and compact breakpoints, use modal drawers instead.

contentChunks.footer: Standard navigation drawer providing access to drawer destinations next to app content
contentChunks.altText: Standard navigation drawer in a mail app with active destination “Inbox” next to app content.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Modal navigation drawer

Modal navigation drawers use a scrim to block interaction with the rest of an app’s content, and don’t affect the screen’s layout grid.

Modal navigation drawers can be used in any breakpoint, but are primarily used in compact and medium sizes where space is limited or prioritized for app content.

They can be swapped with standard drawers on expanded, large, and extra-large breakpoints.

contentChunks.footer: Modal navigation drawer using a scrim to block interaction with the rest of an app’s content
contentChunks.altText: Modal navigation drawer with 1 active destination and scrim.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Modal navigation drawers are always opened by an action outside of the drawer, such as clicking a navigation menu icon in a navigation rail.

Modal drawers can be dismissed by:

  • Selecting a drawer item
  • Tapping the scrim
  • Swiping toward the drawer’s anchoring edge (for example, swiping right-to-left for a left-aligned navigation drawer)

contentChunks.footer: A modal drawer opened by an action such as clicking a navigation menu icon (1)
contentChunks.altText: Diagram noting a navigation menu icon in a navigation rail.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Modal drawers can be dismissed by tapping the scrim or swiping the drawer toward its anchoring screen edge.

contentChunks.footer:
1. Dismiss by tapping the scrim
2. Dismiss by swiping the drawer
contentChunks.altText: 2 modal navigations illustrating tapping the scrim or swiping to dismiss a modal drawer

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Anatomy

Navigation drawers are essentially a list contained within a side sheet. They can also include headers, subheads, and dividers to organize longer lists.

contentChunks.footer:
Navigation drawers can include headers, subheads, and dividers to organize longer lists

  1. Active Indicator
  2. Icon
  3. Label
  4. Badge label
  5. Sheet
  6. Divider
  7. Section label (optional)
  8. Scrim
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer diagram numbering 8 elements.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Sheet

A sheet holds all navigation drawer elements. Side sheets are used as the container for standard and modal navigation drawers.

Navigation drawers that open from the side are always placed on the start edge of the screen, on the left for left-to-right (LTR) languages, and on the right for right-to-left (RTL) languages.

contentChunks.footer: A navigation drawer opens from the left side of the screen for left-to-right languages
contentChunks.altText: Modal navigation drawer opening from left side of screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Divider (optional)

Dividers can be used to separate groups of destinations within the navigation drawer.

contentChunks.footer: Use full-width dividers (1) to separate groups of destinations
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer using horizontal dividers to separate a group of destinations

contentChunks.footer: Don’t use dividers to separate individual destinations
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer using horizontal dividers to separate individual destinations

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Active indicator

The active indicator is a background shape communicating which destination of the navigation drawer is currently being displayed.

contentChunks.footer: The active indicator (1) is a background shape communicating which destination of the navigation drawer is currently being displayed
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer diagram numbering 1 element.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Label text and icons

Destinations in a navigation drawer take the form of actionable list items. Each item describes its destination using label text and an optional icon.

contentChunks.footer: Actionable list items in a navigation drawer describe each destination using (1) an optional icon and (2) required label text
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer diagram numbering 2 elements.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Label text should be clear and short enough that it isn’t cut off by the sheet.

contentChunks.footer: Navigation drawers can use text labels without icons
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer using only label text for 4 destinations. Label text “Inbox” in active destination.

contentChunks.footer: Keep text labels concise, but truncate them if they extend beyond the container width
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer with 1 truncated text label.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t wrap label text
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer with 1 text label with wrapped label text.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t shrink text size in order to fit a text label on a single line
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer with 1 text label featuring smaller text.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Icons can supplement labels as indicators of a destination. When used, they should always be placed before text. Other app components and content should reference these icons.

contentChunks.footer: Use recognizable icons when conventions exist
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer with active destination “Inbox” featuring recognizable icon.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t apply icons to some destinations and not others. Icons should be used for all destinations, or none.
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer with 4 destinations, 2 with text label and icon, 2 with only text label.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Section label (optional)

Short subhead section labels can help group related destinations in the navigation drawer.

contentChunks.footer: Related destinations can be grouped using short subhead section labels in the navigation drawer
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer showing subhead section labels.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Scrim (modal only)

Modal navigation drawers use a scrim to block interaction with the rest of the app. The scrim is placed directly behind the drawer’s sheet and can be tapped or clicked to dismiss the drawer.

contentChunks.footer: Scrim applied behind a modal navigation drawer
contentChunks.altText: Modal navigation drawer with scrim placed behind.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Responsive layout

A product’s navigation component should change to suit the breakpoint and form factor of the screen.

Modal navigation drawers can be used at any breakpoint but are most common in compact and medium breakpoints.

Standard navigation drawers are best for expanded, large, and extra-large breakpoints. 

Use a transition when swapping components. For example, when switching from a portrait to landscape layout, the navigation rail should transform into a navigation drawer.

contentChunks.footer: Standard navigation drawers change size to suit the device’s screen
contentChunks.altText: Navigation rail changing to navigation. drawer on a larger screen

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Compact breakpoint

Use modal navigation drawers in compact breakpoints. Or swap the drawer for a navigation bar.

On web, when the screen size is smaller than 320 CSS pixels, swap the navigation drawer for a navigation bar to ensure accessibility.

contentChunks.footer: Use a modal navigation drawer on mobile screens
contentChunks.altText: Modal navigation drawer with 1 active destination.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Medium & expanded breakpoints

Use a modal navigation drawer alone or with a navigation rail on medium and expanded breakpoints.

When a navigation rail and modal navigation drawer are used together, the drawer can repeat destinations in the navigation rail as long as the drawer offers enough visual separation between levels of the navigation hierarchy.

A standard navigation drawer can be used in single pane layouts in expanded breakpoints.

contentChunks.footer: Use a navigation rail on tablet screens, or also allow a drawer to open and close via a menu icon
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer on tablet with 1 active destination.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Large and extra-large breakpoints

For web experiences on laptop and desktop devices, use either a standard navigation drawer, or a navigation rail that transitions into a modal navigation drawer.

contentChunks.footer: Use a standard navigation drawer on large and desktop screens
contentChunks.altText: Navigation drawer showing 1 active destination.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Behavior

Scrolling

Navigation drawers can be vertically scrolled, independent of the rest of the screen’s content and UI. If the list of navigation destinations is longer than the height of the drawer, the drawer’s contents can be scrolled within the drawer.

contentChunks.footer: When a navigation drawer is scrolled, the body content should remain stationary
contentChunks.altText: A navigation drawer on the left region of an email app is scrolled vertically without disturbing the rest of the content.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Visibility

Dismissible standard drawers can be used for layouts that prioritize content (such as a photo gallery) or for apps where users are unlikely to switch destinations often. They should use a visible navigation menu icon to open and close the drawer.

contentChunks.footer: A standard dismissible navigation drawer is opened and closed by tapping the navigation menu icon in the app bar (1), and remains open until the menu icon is tapped again (2)
contentChunks.altText: Side-by-side standard navigation drawer opened and then closed after tapping menu bar.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Permanently visible standard drawers allow quick navigation between unrelated destinations. They can’t be closed or dismissed by the user.

contentChunks.footer: A permanently-visible standard navigation drawer on desktop
contentChunks.altText: Standard navigation drawer moving between destinations.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Appearing

When a navigation drawer animates on screen, it uses an enter and exit transition pattern.

contentChunks.footer: A navigation drawer animating on screen
contentChunks.altText: In an email app, navigation drawer opens on menu icon click, and closes on outside click.

Use cases

Users should be able to: 

  • Move between navigation destinations with assistive technology
  • Select a particular navigation destination from a set
  • Get appropriate feedback based on input type
Interaction & style

Touch

  • When a navigation item is tapped, the active indicator appears in place, providing feedback to the user that it is selected
  • A touch ripple passes through the indicator
  • The icon switches from outlined to filled
  • The icon changes color, becoming darker

contentChunks.footer: Touch: Tap
contentChunks.altText: Active indicator and other visual cues appear when nav drawers are tapped.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Cursor

  • When hovered, the hover indicator appears providing a visual cue that the destination is interactive
  • When clicked, a ripple passes through the indicator
  • The icon switches from outlined to filled
  • The icon changes color, becoming darker in light theme and lighter in dark theme, to increase the contrast

contentChunks.footer: Cursor: Hover, Click
contentChunks.altText: When a cursor goes over a navigation drawer, a hover indicator appears. When tapped, the active indicator appears.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Initial focus
Initial focus lands directly on the first navigation item, since that is the first interactive element of the component.

contentChunks.footer: Focus lands on first navigation item
contentChunks.altText: 1. Tab lands on the first navigation item, Inbox. 2. Down arrow to get to the second navigation item, Outbox.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Closing
The modal navigation drawer can be dismissed by selecting the scrim that covers the rest of the screen.

contentChunks.footer: Select the scrim to close the navigation drawer
contentChunks.altText: A navigation drawer with a scrim covering the body content. A touch target is selecting the scrim.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Visual indicators

Icons are the primary focus of the navigation and such give the dominant cue of its state. Use a filled icon for the selected destination to differentiate from the outlined icons of non-selected destinations.

contentChunks.footer: The navigation item is selected via Space/Enter
contentChunks.altText: Space + enter is used to select the navigation item inbox.

contentChunks.footer: Use a filled icon for the selected navigation destination to differentiate from the other destinations
contentChunks.altText: A navigation drawer with the home destination using a filled icon.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid keeping the icon style for the selected navigation destination the same as unselected destination's icons. This removes an important visual indicator of which destination is active.
contentChunks.altText: A navigation drawer with the home destination using an outlined icon.

contentChunks.footer: When selected, the icon fills, darkens in light theme (or lightens in dark theme), and is backed by an active indicator shape
contentChunks.altText: A selected home icon using a filled icon and active indicator and a unselected home icon using an outlined icon.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Keyboard navigation

KeysActions
TabFocus lands on the first navigation destination 
Space or EnterSelects the focused navigation destination, and focus moves to the newly opened section (if applicable)
ArrowNavigate between destinations within the navigation drawer
Labeling elements

The accessibility label for a navigation item is typically the same as the destination name.

If the UI text is correctly linked, assistive tech (such as a screenreader) will read the UI text followed by the component’s role.

For Android Views (MDC-Android), a more descriptive accessibility label is not available to be set and the role is not announced.

contentChunks.footer: A navigation drawer’s accessibility label can incorporate its adjacent UI text
contentChunks.altText: A navigation drawer item’s label text and accessibility label both read “photos.” The role is “tab.”

contentChunks.htmlValue: When the visible UI text is ambiguous, accessibility labels need to be more descriptive. For example, a navigation destination visibly labeled Recents would benefit from additional information in its accessibility label to clarify the destination’s intent.

contentChunks.footer: While the visible label text reads Recents, the accessibility label for this destination clarifies its function: Recent images
contentChunks.altText: A navigation drawer item’s label text is “recents”, the accessibility label is “recent images.” The role is “tab.”
